seo.metaDescription: Moving from 0.9 to 1.0: the breaking changes with the code before and after, and what is new.

props.markdown: This page lists what changes when you move from 0.9 to 1.0. Each breaking change shows the 0.9 code, then a live example of the 1.0 code. The additive changes need no action. For what 1.x keeps stable, see [Stability](/docs/stability).
Five changes can break a build or change what a chart draws. Go through them in order.

In the library, solid is an actual value and hatch is a plan or a reference. A bare `<RankedBars>` now draws solid bars; in 0.9 it drew hatched ones. RankedBars: pass `fill="hatch"` to keep the old look.
After:

props.text: Small pieces are never pink by default

props.markdown:
Pink means loss, and the library only draws it when you ask. Four small pieces were pink or hatched with no props, even when nothing was lost. In 1.0 they use the accent color, and solid is an actual value:

- `InlineBar`: `tone` is `'accent'` (was `'loss'`) and `fill` is `'solid'` (was `'hatch'`).
- `Meter`: `fill` is `'solid'` (was `'hatch'`).
- `RangeMeter`: `tone` is `'accent'` (was `'loss'`) and `referenceTone` is `'neutral'` (was `'accent'`). The hatched gap stays.
- `DotCount`: `tone` is `'accent'` (was `'loss'`).

To keep the 0.9 look, pass the old values.

props.code:
<InlineBar value={12.3} max={40} label="Margin" />
<Meter value={34} min={20} max={45} label="Gross margin" />
<RangeMeter value={12.3} reference={36} max={40} label="Margin" />
<DotCount count={29} />

props.markdown: After, with the old look pinned:

props.code:
<InlineBar value={12.3} max={40} tone="loss" fill="hatch" label="Margin" />
<Meter value={34} min={20} max={45} fill="hatch" label="Gross margin" />
<RangeMeter value={12.3} reference={36} max={40} tone="loss" referenceTone="accent" label="Margin" />
<DotCount count={29} tone="loss" />

props.text: A chart needs a title or aria-labelledby

props.markdown: `Chart` and the 11 high-level charts now require an accessible name in their types: a `title`, or an `aria-labelledby` that points at an element naming the chart. A chart with neither is a type error. The development warning stays for calls from JavaScript. With both props, `aria-labelledby` names the chart and `title` stays the default caption of the data table.
After, with a `title`:
After, with a heading that already names the chart. `aria-labelledby` points at the id of the heading:

`ChartProps` and every `*Props` of the 11 charts are now type aliases, an intersection with the new exported type `ChartName`, not interfaces. So `interface … extends BarChartProps<D>` no longer compiles. Use `type … = BarChartProps<D> & {…}`:

Do not wrap a props type in `Pick` or `Omit`. They collapse the union of `ChartName` and the chart loses the requirement of a name. If you must, add it back with `& ChartName`: `type MyProps<D> = Omit<BarChartProps<D>, 'height'> & ChartName`.

props.text: An invalid date breaks the line

props.markdown: `Area` and `LineChart` no longer join the line, band or area across a date that isn’t a date, or across a missing value. They break there, as `Line` and `Band` already did: a series with a bad date in the middle draws two segments instead of one. To keep the old joined line, filter the rows before you pass them. The same filter keeps an `Area` joined; for a missing value, filter out the rows whose value is `null` or `NaN`.
After:

The wording of the strings the library writes itself, such as the keyboard hint, is not part of the public API and can change in a minor release (see [Stability](/docs/stability)). Pass your own `keyboardHint`, or another text you control, wherever you need to know the exact words, and use [`ChartsProvider messages`](/docs/hooks-and-providers#messages) to translate any of them by key. In tests, don’t search by the built-in text: find the chart by its `title` and role.

props.code: expect(screen.getByText('Use arrow keys to move between points, Home and End for first and last, Escape to clear.')).toBeInTheDocument()

props.markdown: After: a `keyboardHint` you pass is used as is, so you can assert on it.
These need no action. They are new in 1.0.
`LineChart` takes an `underlay`: an element drawn after the grid and before the lines, for example an `Area` with last year’s values. See [LineChart](/docs/line-chart) for the props.

`createDateFormatter(spec, options)` builds a function from epoch milliseconds to a string, in `'day'`, `'month'`, `'quarter'`, `'year'`, `'auto'` or any `Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions`. It is exported from `tally-charts/core` with three types: `DateFormatSpec` for the first argument, `DateFormatOptions` for the second and `DateFormatter` for the result. See [Formatting](/docs/formatting).

props.text: The Enter hint only on selectable points

props.markdown: The keyboard hint adds “Press Enter to select.” only while the active point can be selected: the chart has `onSelect` and the point doesn’t have `selectable: false`. In 0.9 the sentence could promise Enter on a chart where it did nothing. Tab into the chart below and listen; remove `onSelect` and the sentence is gone.

- `ChartsProvider messages`: every built-in string in your language, by key. See [Translating the built-in text](/docs/hooks-and-providers#messages).
- `Sparkline`: a line of values for KPI rows and table cells, with no measuring and no effects. See [Small pieces](/docs/small-pieces).
- `y2` on `Chart`, `scale="y2"` on `Line`, `Area`, `Band`, `Bars`, `ValueLabel`, `Target` and `Axis`, and `tone` on `Axis`. See [Two value axes](/docs/composition#dual-axis).
- `position` on `Target`, to place a rule within a category of a band or point scale, and `y` as a category. See [Composition](/docs/composition).
- A reversed `y` scale, `y={{ domain: [10, 1] }}`, is now documented behaviour. See [Composition](/docs/composition).
- `color` on `ShareBar` segments, `Legend` items and solid `Bars`, for any CSS colour outside the tones.
- `width` on `InlineBar` takes a string, so `width="100%"` works. See [Small pieces](/docs/small-pieces).
- `at="max"` and `variant="pill"` on `ValueLabel`; `valueLabel="max"` and `valueLabelVariant` on `BarChart`.
- `interactive` on `LineChart`: `interactive={false}` draws a static chart. See [LineChart](/docs/line-chart).
If you come from before 0.9, these changes still apply. The full history is in the [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/mwadon/tally-charts/blob/main/packages/tally-charts/CHANGELOG.md).

0.6 froze the public API. Every rename, before → after:

- `<LineChart axis={…} axisFormat={…}>` → `<LineChart yAxis={…} yAxisFormat={…}>`, plus a new `xAxisFormat`.
- The type of `<LineChart band={…}>`, `LineRange` → `LineBand`.
- `<Bars tooltip={(d) => segments}>` → `<Bars segments={(d) => segments}>`.
- `<ComparisonBars overIsBad={false}>` → `<ComparisonBars good="up">` (the default is `good="down"`); `onPlanText` → `onPlanLabel`.
- `useChart('MyMark')` → `useChart()`, which returns only the public fields (`chartId`, `warn`, `radius`, `registerPoints` and `unregisterPoints` are gone).
- `useRegisterPoints(ctx, points)` → `useRegisterPoints(points)`.
- `ctx.x.scale` and `ctx.y.scale` are the library's own `LinearScale`, `BandScale`, `PointScale` and `TimeScale`. D3-only methods such as `.copy()` are gone, and d3-scale is no longer a dependency.
- Axis format functions get an `AxisValue` (`string | number | Date`): `(v: string | number) => string` → `(v: AxisValue) => string`, or drop the annotation.
- The types `ComparisonStatus`, `WaterfallKind` and `DeltaDirection` are no longer exported. Use string literals.
- `tally-charts/core` keeps only formatting, `thresholds`, `heatmapLevel`, `toNumber`, `toTime` and the shared and scale types. `createScale`, `computeBars`, `categoryTicks` and the other layout helpers, `createWarner` and `isDev` are internal now.
- CSS: style `[data-ch-part="…"]`, not classes (`.ch-pill-seg` → `[data-ch-part="pill-segment"]`, `.ch-swatch` → `[data-ch-part="legend-swatch"]`, …). `--ch-swatch-color`, `--ch-range-ref-color`, `--ch-heatmap-columns` and `--ch-seq-ink-strong` became private `--_ch-*` variables. `[data-ch-dir]` on bars → `[data-ch-direction]`, as on `Delta`.
- Percent and pts axes drop their decimals when every tick is whole: "0%", not "0.0%".
- `Chart` (and so every high-level chart) and `Heatmap` warn in development when `title` is missing.

props.code: <LineChart data={rows} x="year" series={series} axis="currency" axisFormat={(v: string | number) => String(v)} />
<LineChart data={rows} x="year" series={series} yAxis="currency" yAxisFormat={(v: AxisValue) => String(v)} />

props.markdown:
These need no code change, but tests and custom styles may notice them:

- The chart's focus, keys and `aria-*` moved from the `<figure>` to the plot inside it (`[data-ch-part="plot"]`, `role="application"`). Tests that focus or send keys to the figure should use `getByRole('application')`. The focus ring is on the plot.
- Announcements start with the position: "Jul 6, 37.5%" → "1 of 12, Jul 6, 37.5%", and with the series when there are several. `StripPlot` point labels no longer repeat the series name.
- Data tables head each row with its first cell, read empty values as "no value", and use field names in sentence case ("week" → "Week").
- Toned text (row and value labels, bridge notes, waffle group labels, pill values) mixes the tone with ink, keyed on `data-ch-tone-text`. The `ch-tone-text` class is gone.
- Light `--ch-warn` is `#be802f` (was `#f1a23b`), `--ch-gain` `#22a363` (`#23a866`) and `--ch-neutral` `#8e8e95` (`#a3a3ab`). Hatched and soft-accent marks have a 1px outline in both themes. [Palettes](/docs/palettes) has the old colors as `vivid`.
- The sequential levels have new shares per tone and theme, and the dark top level is the pure base with dark text. `data-ch-seq-tone` now also sets `--ch-seq-base`.
- `Heatmap` column headers hold only the names. The column totals are a row of their own (`[data-ch-part="heatmap-total-row"]`), ending with the grand total, so 0.6's `heatmap-header-total` part is gone. The grid sits in `[data-ch-part="heatmap-scroll"]`.
- `WaffleColumns`' default top margin is 44px when it pins the peak pill (8px before), so the pill no longer sits on the tallest column.
- An axis keeps only its first label when even its first and last would overlap. Every value stays reachable through the tooltip and the data table.

Nothing was removed in 0.8 and 0.9, they only added to the API.

- 0.6: time scales, `ChartPoint<D>` in callbacks, a function `tooltip` on high-level charts, `{ preset, digits, signed }` formats, `axisFormat` on `BarChart` and `DotHistogram`, `chartId` on `Heatmap`, `heatmapLevel`, and readonly arrays everywhere.
- 0.6b: `keyboardHint` on every chart, `rowLabel` on `Heatmap`, `dataTable={{ caption, columns }}` on high-level charts, `layout` on `ComparisonBars`, `marker` and `shape: 'band'` on `Legend` items, `series` on `ChartPoint` and `DotItem`, the `--ch-heatmap-min-cell` token, the parts `plot`, `heatmap-total-row`, `heatmap-scroll`, `meter-min-label`, `range-scale-min` and `range-scale-max`, and the state attributes `data-ch-tone-text`, `data-ch-peak` and `data-ch-marker`.
- 0.8: `ShareBar` and `ZoneMeter`. See [Small pieces](/docs/small-pieces).
- 0.9: `thresholds(…, { inclusive: 'upper' })`, plain `{ bins, inclusive }` zones on `ZoneMeter`, and `selectable` on `RankedBars`, `Bars` and `ChartPoint`. See [Thresholds](/docs/thresholds).
